text: Thank you for those details; the radiation to your arm and jaw combined with sweating is very concerning for cardiac ischemia. Has this pain ever occurred at rest, or does it strictly happen during physical exertion? Also, how long do these episodes typically last?

speaker: Patient
text: It usually only happens when I'm pushing heavy loads or climbing stairs, but it doesn't seem to start while I'm sitting still. The tightness typically lasts for about five to ten minutes before it passes completely.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That pattern of exertional angina lasting 5-10 minutes is classic for stable coronary artery disease, but we must rule out acute instability. REQUEST TEST: Electrocardiogram (ECG). Have you ever been diagnosed with high blood pressure, high cholesterol, or diabetes?

REQUEST TEST: Lipid_Profile. Do you currently smoke, or have you had any recent trauma to your chest?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electrocardiogram: ST segment depression in leads I, AVL, V4-V6 suggestive of ischemia. Lipid Profile: Total Cholesterol 250 mg/dL (elevated), LDL 160 mg/dL (elevated), HDL 40 mg/dL, Triglycerides 180 mg/dL.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Stable Angina Pectoris secondary to Coronary Artery Disease.

Given the ECG showing ischemia, elevated cholesterol, and your classic symptoms, I recommend starting aspirin and a beta-blocker immediately and scheduling a stress test to assess the severity of the blockage. Do you have any family history of early heart attacks or strokes?
